items.title: Linear algebra
items.why: Vectors, matrices, eigenvectors, and matrix factorizations make model representations and transformations easier to reason about.

items.title: Probability and statistics
items.why: Random variables, likelihood, expectation, and uncertainty underpin estimation, loss functions, and evaluation.

items.title: Calculus and gradients
items.why: Derivatives, chain rule, and gradients explain how backpropagation computes parameter updates.

items.title: Optimization basics
items.why: Objective functions, constraints, and gradient descent provide the language for fitting machine-learning models.

items.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
items.why: XGBoost made regularized gradient tree boosting practical at scale, with a system design that exposes the cost and accuracy trade-offs.

items.title: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features
items.why: CatBoost addresses categorical features and prediction shift with ordered boosting, making its training choices the central lesson.

items.title: A Tutorial on Principal Component Analysis
items.why: This tutorial develops principal component analysis from covariance structure through eigenvectors, low-rank approximation, and practical interpretation.

items.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
items.venue: FAT* '19: Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, January 29--31, 2019, Atlanta, GA, USA
items.why: Model Cards proposes a concise reporting format for intended use, evaluation conditions, and limitations of trained models.

items.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
items.why: Adam combines adaptive first- and second-moment estimates into a simple stochastic optimizer that became a common neural-network baseline.

items.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
items.why: Batch Normalization stabilizes layer input distributions during training and enables faster optimization at higher learning rates.

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.why: ResNet introduces identity shortcuts that let very deep convolutional networks train effectively, reframing depth as an optimization problem.

items.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
items.why: VGG demonstrates the representational strength of deep networks built from repeated small convolution filters and simple design choices.

items.title: Optimization Methods for Large-Scale Machine Learning
items.why: This work surveys optimization methods for large-scale machine learning, emphasizing how computational structure shapes practical optimizer choices.

items.title: Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet and the Impact of Residual Connections on Learning
items.why: Inception-v4 and Inception-ResNet study efficient convolutional architectures and the effect of residual connections inside Inception modules.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.why: The Transformer replaces recurrence with attention and shows that sequence modeling can be parallelized while retaining strong translation quality.

items.title: Equilibrated adaptive learning rates for non-convex optimization
items.why: The paper analyzes how optimization and generalization interact in deep learning, arguing that successful training dynamics need not imply classical overfitting.

items.title: Accurate, Large Minibatch SGD: Training ImageNet in 1 Hour
items.why: The work demonstrates large-minibatch stochastic gradient descent for ImageNet and describes the linear learning-rate scaling and warmup recipe.

items.title: Deep Neural Networks as Gaussian Processes
items.why: This work connects infinitely wide deep neural networks to Gaussian processes, providing a kernel view of network initialization and prediction.

items.title: Averaging Weights Leads to Wider Optima and Better Generalization
items.why: The authors show that averaging model weights can lead to wider optima and improve generalization in deep learning.

items.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
items.venue: In Advances in neural information processing systems (pp. 8571-8580) 2018
items.why: The Neural Tangent Kernel characterizes gradient-descent training of wide neural networks and gives a tractable account of convergence and generalization.

items.title: On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond
items.why: This paper analyzes convergence properties of Adam and proposes an update that addresses cases where the original method can fail to converge.

items.title: Adafactor: Adaptive Learning Rates with Sublinear Memory Cost
items.why: Adafactor reduces optimizer-state memory by factoring second-moment estimates, making adaptive optimization more practical for large models.

items.title: Symbolic Discovery of Optimization Algorithms
items.why: Lion introduces a simple sign-based optimizer discovered through symbolic search and evaluates its memory and training trade-offs.

items.title: Learning Rates as a Function of Batch Size: A Random Matrix Theory Approach to Neural Network Training
items.why: This paper studies the geometry of neural-network loss surfaces and shows how the Hessian spectrum changes during training.

items.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
items.why: The Variational Autoencoder gives a scalable variational-inference objective for learning a probabilistic latent representation with neural networks.

items.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
items.why: GANs formulate generative learning as a minimax game between a generator and discriminator, introducing an influential implicit-density approach.

items.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics
items.why: DCGAN identifies architectural guidelines that make convolutional GAN representations more stable and useful for image generation.

items.title: Improved Techniques for Training GANs
items.why: The paper studies practical GAN training techniques, including feature matching, minibatch discrimination, and historical averaging.

items.title: InfoVAE: Information Maximizing Variational Autoencoders
items.why: InfoVAE modifies the variational autoencoder objective to control mutual information and improve the informativeness of latent representations.

items.title: Understanding disentangling in $β$-VAE
items.why: The authors propose a mutual-information objective for unsupervised visual representation learning, connecting augmentation-based prediction to invariance.

items.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
items.why: SimCLR demonstrates a simple contrastive-learning framework whose performance depends strongly on augmentations, projection heads, and large batches.

items.title: Exploring Simple Siamese Representation Learning
items.why: This work presents momentum contrast with a queue and momentum encoder, enabling contrastive visual learning with many negatives and modest batches.

items.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
items.why: The paper introduces efficient continuous vector representations of words and training objectives that capture useful linguistic regularities.

items.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
items.why: Sequence-to-sequence learning maps an input sequence to an output sequence with an encoder-decoder recurrent neural network.

items.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
items.why: The authors introduce attention for neural machine translation so the decoder can selectively use source positions instead of a fixed-length encoding.

items.title: Layer Normalization
items.why: Layer Normalization normalizes hidden activations within each training example, avoiding dependence on batch statistics.

items.title: Deep contextualized word representations
items.why: ULMFiT shows how general-domain language-model pretraining can be fine-tuned effectively for text classification tasks.

items.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
items.why: BERT pretrains bidirectional Transformer representations and establishes a broadly reusable fine-tuning recipe for language understanding.

items.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
items.why: Transformer-XL extends attention with recurrence and relative positional representations to model dependencies beyond a fixed segment.

items.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
items.why: RoBERTa revisits BERT's training recipe and shows that data, training duration, and optimization choices substantially affect results.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.why: The paper studies scaling laws for language models, relating model size, data, and compute to predictable loss trends.

items.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
items.why: T5 frames NLP tasks as text-to-text problems and compares transfer-learning objectives and model scales in one unified setup.

items.title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
items.why: ELECTRA trains a discriminator to identify replaced tokens, obtaining an efficient alternative to masked-language-model pretraining.

items.title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
items.why: Longformer combines local windowed attention with task-driven global attention to handle longer documents efficiently.

items.title: Efficient Transformers: A Survey
items.why: This survey organizes efficient Transformer variants by how they reduce attention's compute or memory cost on long sequences.

items.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
items.why: Vision Transformer applies a standard Transformer to image patches and shows that large-scale pretraining can make this design competitive.

items.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
items.why: Swin Transformer uses shifted windows to build hierarchical visual features with attention whose cost scales linearly with image size.

items.title: A ConvNet for the 2020s
items.why: ConvNeXt modernizes a pure convolutional architecture using design choices informed by contemporary Transformer networks.

items.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
items.why: Focal Loss reshapes dense object-detection training to focus on hard examples under severe foreground-background class imbalance.

items.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
items.why: You Only Look Once formulates object detection as a single regression problem, enabling fast end-to-end prediction from an image.

items.title: R-FCN: Object Detection via Region-based Fully Convolutional Networks
items.why: R-FCN uses position-sensitive score maps to share most computation across regions while retaining localization for object detection.

items.title: Rethinking ImageNet Pre-training
items.why: This study revisits ImageNet pretraining and reports how pretraining choices affect transfer to downstream vision tasks.

items.title: YOLOv3: An Incremental Improvement
items.why: YOLOv3 improves a one-stage detector with multi-scale predictions and a stronger feature extractor while preserving fast inference.

items.title: Objects as Points
items.why: Objects as Points formulates object detection as predicting object centers and regressing their attributes from a heatmap.

items.title: Mask R-CNN
items.why: Mask R-CNN adds a parallel mask-prediction branch to object detection and extends the region-based framework to instance segmentation.

items.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
items.why: Feature Pyramid Networks build semantically strong multi-scale feature maps with a top-down pathway and lateral connections for object detection.

items.title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention
items.why: DeiT shows that data-efficient training and distillation can make vision Transformers work well without massive private datasets.

items.title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation
items.why: Mask2Former unifies several image-segmentation tasks with masked attention over image features and predicted regions.

items.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.why: DDPM connects denoising diffusion training to variational inference and shows high-quality image generation through a simple noise-prediction objective.

items.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
items.why: The score-SDE framework unifies discrete and continuous diffusion models and derives sampling methods from stochastic differential equations.

items.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
items.why: Latent Diffusion moves denoising into a learned perceptual latent space, reducing compute while retaining high-resolution synthesis quality.

items.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding
items.why: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding scales a language encoder and cascaded diffusion for text-conditioned image synthesis.

items.title: eDiff-I: Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with an Ensemble of Expert Denoisers
items.why: eDiff-I uses an ensemble of expert denoisers specialized to different noise ranges to improve text-to-image diffusion quality.

items.title: Simple diffusion: End-to-end diffusion for high resolution images
items.why: Simple Diffusion studies an end-to-end diffusion design for high-resolution generation, including choices that simplify the model pipeline.

items.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models
items.why: Elucidating the Design Space analyzes diffusion parameterizations, noise schedules, and samplers to clarify quality and speed trade-offs.

items.title: Improved Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.why: Improved DDPM proposes learned reverse-process variances and a new schedule to improve diffusion likelihoods and sampling efficiency.

items.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.why: The DQN work combines deep convolutional perception with Q-learning and replay to learn control policies directly from Atari pixels.

items.title: Continuous control with deep reinforcement learning
items.why: This paper introduces deep deterministic policy gradients for continuous control, combining an actor-critic method with replay and target networks.

items.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
items.why: PPO constrains policy updates with a clipped surrogate objective, making repeated minibatch optimization practical for policy-gradient learning.

items.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
items.why: Soft Actor-Critic derives a maximum-entropy off-policy actor-critic algorithm that balances reward and policy entropy.

items.title: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods
items.why: TD3 addresses value overestimation in continuous control with clipped double critics, delayed policy updates, and target smoothing.

items.title: OpenAI Gym
items.why: OpenAI Gym provides a common toolkit and benchmark interface for comparing reinforcement-learning algorithms across environments.

items.title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
items.why: Decision Transformer treats offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling over states, actions, and desired returns.

items.title: What Matters In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning? A Large-Scale Empirical Study
items.why: This large-scale empirical study tests implementation and hyperparameter choices that matter for on-policy reinforcement-learning results.

items.title: D4RL: Datasets for Deep Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning
items.why: D4RL provides benchmark tasks for offline reinforcement learning and highlights dataset quality and evaluation challenges.

items.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
items.why: GPT-3 demonstrates that scaling autoregressive language models improves few-shot task performance through in-context examples.

items.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
items.why: Chinchilla argues that compute-optimal language-model training requires scaling tokens alongside parameters, revising common model-size choices.

items.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
items.why: PaLM studies scaling a dense decoder-only language model and reports performance across reasoning, multilingual, and code tasks.

items.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
items.why: BLOOM documents the training and release of a multilingual large language model, including its data governance and evaluation approach.

items.title: OPT: Open Pre-trained Transformer Language Models
items.why: OPT presents a family of openly available decoder-only language models and documents reproducible training and evaluation choices.

items.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
items.why: The LLaMA family reports strong results from training dense language models on more tokens, emphasizing data and training efficiency.

items.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
items.why: Llama 2 documents a family of pretrained and instruction-tuned models and reports its data, safety, and evaluation methodology.

items.title: Mistral 7B
items.why: Mistral 7B combines grouped-query attention and sliding-window attention and reports strong performance at a compact model scale.

items.title: Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models
items.why: Gemini reports a family of multimodal models trained to understand and combine text, image, audio, video, and code inputs.

items.title: Gemma: Open Models Based on Gemini Research and Technology
items.why: Gemma presents openly available lightweight language models and describes training data, evaluation, and responsible-use guidance.

items.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
items.why: InstructGPT studies supervised demonstrations and human-feedback reinforcement learning as a way to make language models follow instructions.

items.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.why: Constitutional AI uses written principles and AI feedback to supervise and align assistants while reducing dependence on human labels.

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
items.why: DPO derives a direct preference-optimization objective that fits a preference model without a separate online RL loop.

items.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
items.why: DeepSeekMath introduces GRPO, a group-relative policy optimization method, and applies it to mathematical reasoning in language models.

items.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
items.venue: Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235:26874-26901, 2024
items.why: RLAIF vs. RLHF compares AI feedback and human feedback as sources of preference supervision for reinforcement learning from feedback.

items.title: Back to Basics: Revisiting REINFORCE Style Optimization for Learning from Human Feedback in LLMs
items.why: This paper revisits REINFORCE-style policy optimization for human-feedback language-model training and evaluates a simpler alternative to PPO.

items.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
items.why: SimPO proposes a reference-free preference-optimization objective with length-normalized rewards for aligning language models.

items.title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part I: PPO
items.why: The paper examines reward-model overoptimization and proposes a proxy-aware approach to reduce failures from optimizing imperfect preferences.

items.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
items.why: FlashAttention uses IO-aware tiling to compute exact attention with less high-bandwidth-memory traffic and lower memory use.

items.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
items.why: PagedAttention manages the KV cache in non-contiguous blocks, enabling higher-throughput LLM serving through virtual-memory-inspired allocation.

items.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
items.why: Grouped-Query Attention shares key-value heads across query groups to reduce autoregressive inference cost while retaining quality.

items.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need
items.why: Multi-Query Attention shares keys and values across attention heads to reduce memory bandwidth during incremental decoding.

items.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
items.why: GPTQ presents post-training weight quantization using approximate second-order information to compress large language models.

items.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
items.why: AWQ protects salient weights during low-bit quantization and demonstrates efficient inference for large language models.

items.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
items.why: Speculative decoding uses a small draft model to propose tokens that a larger target model verifies in parallel without changing output distributions.

items.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.why: LoRA reduces fine-tuning memory and trainable parameters with low-rank weight updates that can be merged into the base model.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.why: RAG combines parametric generation with a retrieved non-parametric memory, grounding generation in external passages.

items.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
items.why: Dense Passage Retrieval trains dual encoders for open-domain question answering and establishes a strong learned retrieval baseline.

items.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
items.why: ColBERT uses late interaction between contextualized query and document tokens to balance retrieval effectiveness and indexability.

items.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
items.why: This work studies zero-shot dense retrieval without relevance labels and examines pseudo-relevance feedback for improving ranking.

items.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
items.why: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with actions, showing how language models can use tools and observations in a loop.

items.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
items.why: Toolformer explores self-supervised tool-use learning by letting a language model decide when and how to call APIs.

items.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.why: Reflexion uses verbal feedback and episodic memory to improve an agent's future decisions without updating model weights.

items.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
items.why: Gorilla studies retrieval-aware API selection and fine-tuning for language models that need to call rapidly changing tools.

items.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
items.why: CLIP learns transferable image representations from natural-language supervision collected at scale.

items.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
items.why: Flamingo connects frozen vision and language models with gated cross-attention to support few-shot multimodal tasks.

items.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
items.why: BLIP-2 bridges frozen image encoders and language models with a lightweight Querying Transformer.

items.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
items.why: LLaVA instruction-tunes a language model on multimodal conversations generated from image-text data.

items.title: ImageBind: One Embedding Space To Bind Them All
items.why: ImageBind learns a shared embedding space across six modalities using image-paired data as the binding signal.

items.title: Qwen-VL: A Versatile Vision-Language Model for Understanding, Localization, Text Reading, and Beyond
items.why: Qwen-VL studies visual-language alignment and resolution handling for general-purpose image understanding and dialogue.

items.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
items.why: SigLIP replaces the global contrastive softmax with a pairwise sigmoid loss for language-image pretraining.

items.title: Video-LLaVA: Learning United Visual Representation by Alignment Before Projection
items.why: Video-LLaVA aligns visual representations from images and video to support unified video-language understanding.

items.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
items.why: The graph convolutional network paper applies localized spectral graph convolutions to semi-supervised node classification.

items.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
items.why: GraphSAGE learns an inductive neighborhood-aggregation function so embeddings can be generated for unseen nodes.

items.title: Graph Attention Networks
items.why: Graph Attention Networks use masked self-attention to weight neighborhood messages in graph representation learning.

items.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
items.why: The sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts layer increases model capacity through conditional computation and learned expert routing.

items.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
items.why: Switch Transformers simplify sparse expert routing and demonstrate scaling language-model capacity with modest additional compute.

items.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
items.why: DeepSeekMoE studies fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts to improve specialization and parameter efficiency.

items.title: Toy Models of Superposition
items.why: This paper analyzes superposition in neural networks, explaining how models can represent more features than they have dimensions.

tracks.title: ML research foundations (beginner)
tracks.audience: Learners beginning ML who want a grounded route from mathematical tools to modern learned representations.
assumedKnowledge: Comfort with algebra; calculus and probability can be learned alongside the track.
outcomes: Explain core supervised-learning and neural-network ideas
Read foundational ML papers and identify their claims
Choose a next specialization based on learned concepts

tracks.title: Transformers & LLMs
tracks.audience: Learners who want to understand language-model architecture, pretraining, post-training, and serving.
assumedKnowledge: Linear algebra and gradient descent, or completion of ML research foundations
outcomes: Trace a Transformer language-model pipeline
Compare pretraining and alignment objectives
Explain the main compute and memory trade-offs in inference

tracks.title: Reinforcement learning to RLHF/GRPO
tracks.audience: Learners moving from value-based and policy-gradient RL toward preference optimization for language models.
outcomes: Compare value-based, policy-gradient, and offline RL
Explain PPO and group-relative optimization
Describe how feedback objectives connect to assistant alignment

tracks.title: Generative models & diffusion
tracks.audience: Learners interested in the foundations and modern design choices behind generative models.
assumedKnowledge: Probability, neural networks, and basic optimization
outcomes: Contrast adversarial, latent-variable, and diffusion approaches
Explain denoising objectives and sampling
Identify the role of latent spaces and guidance

tracks.title: Computer vision
tracks.audience: Learners who want a route through image recognition, detection, segmentation, and modern vision Transformers.
outcomes: Explain convolutional and attention-based vision models
Compare classification, detection, and segmentation architectures
Interpret compute-aware vision design choices

tracks.title: Efficient inference
tracks.audience: Practitioners focused on reducing LLM inference latency, memory use, or serving cost.
assumedKnowledge: Transformer basics and familiarity with GPU memory concepts
outcomes: Explain KV-cache and attention bottlenecks
Compare quantization and speculative decoding
Reason about memory-aware serving techniques

tracks.title: Retrieval & agents
tracks.audience: Builders studying retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, and agent reasoning loops.
outcomes: Describe dense retrieval and late interaction
Trace a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline
Compare tool-use and reflection patterns in agents

tracks.title: Multimodal learning
tracks.audience: Learners exploring systems that connect images, video, and language.
outcomes: Explain shared embedding and cross-attention approaches
Compare multimodal pretraining and instruction tuning
Identify alignment and evaluation challenges
